title: Feature-flag gating and old-vs-new builder pattern conventions in pkg/registry
answers: Where should feature-flag gating for a new app go?
Should I use builder.APIGroupBuilder or App-SDK app.Provider for a new API?
body:
Feature-flag gating for apps happens in the aggregator ProvideAppInstallers (pkg/registry/apps/apps.go), via features.IsEnabledGlobally(...) checks, not inside the app itself — new experimental apps should follow that pattern rather than self-disabling.
Two API-integration patterns coexist deliberately: raw builder.APIGroupBuilder (older, under apis/) vs App-SDK app.Provider/AppInstaller (newer, under apps/). Check which pattern neighboring code in your domain uses before picking one. ProvideBuilderRunners (pkg/registry/apps/apps.go) is explicitly marked deprecated in favor of ProvideAppInstallers.
WireSetExts in pkg/registry/apis/wireset.go exists so enterprise builds can override OSS defaults (noop role/permission/auditing providers) — don't hardcode enterprise-only wiring into the OSS WireSet.
applies: Applies when adding a new app under pkg/registry/apps/ or deciding between builder.APIGroupBuilder and App-SDK app.Provider for a new integration. Does not apply to backgroundsvcs/usagestatssvcs which have no such split.
